_comment: REFERENCE IMAGES FOR THE MESH PIPELINE, in imagegen.py's own schema so
imagegen validates them with its own rules rather than a second copy of
them living here. tools/meshgen/specs/props-trellis-01.json names these
image ids; nothing else reads this file.
THIS BATCH HAS NEVER BEEN GENERATED, and on the machine this project has
it should not be: TRELLIS cannot run on an AMD card, so making twelve
images for a mesh stage that will refuse them is GPU hours spent on
nothing. meshgen.py runs the probe FIRST and never reaches stage 1 unless
stage 2 can run - the same order imagegen uses to decide before it
downloads 6.7 GB.
WHY THESE TWELVE. They are what a British port town needs and what the CC0
kits in ledger/Assets/Props do not contain: the kits give benches, bins,
bollards, pallets, barrels, crates, cones, chimney pots and a lamp post.
A telephone kiosk, a pillar box, a mooring bollard, creels, fenders and a
belisha beacon are the difference between a generic street and Meridian.
THE FRAMING IS FOR IMAGE-TO-3D, NOT FOR A WALL. A single object, isolated,
whole in frame, evenly lit, on a plain background: that is what a
reconstruction model can use. The signage batch's straight-on elevation
framing would give a flat plate.
SETTING: Meridian is a British port town in the LATE-ANALOG eighties and
nineties. Landlines, cash, paper. Not the 1950s.
NEGATIVES ARE RECORDED AND INERT AT cfg 1.0 - the same measured fact
prompts.json records: sd-cli only evaluates the unconditional branch when
cfg != 1.0, and Z-Image-Turbo is distilled for 1.0. They are written
correctly (nouns, not refusals) so they start acting the day cfg moves.

content_rules.rules_clause: invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness

_comment: Isolated-object framing. `by_kind.prop` overrides both halves,
because the shared signage style asks for a straight-on flat
elevation of a wall and that is the opposite of what an
image-to-3D model needs.
style.prefix: photograph, straight-on flat elevation, evenly lit,
style.suffix: British port town, late 1980s, overcast North Sea daylight

prop.prefix: product photograph of one single object alone, centred on a plain flat mid-grey seamless backdrop, three-quarter view from slightly above, the whole object inside the frame with clear margins, soft even studio lighting from every side,
prop.suffix: British port town, late 1980s, damp salt-weathered paintwork, soot and grime, matte surfaces, sharp focus throughout the object, uniform illumination, plain empty backdrop

_comment: Nouns to push away, never sentences of refusal - a negative
prompt reading `no shadow` asks to push away the phrase.
Inert at cfg 1.0; see the batch comment.
negatives.default: watermark, signature, oversaturated, hdr, colour cast, people, person, hands, face, crowd, cars, traffic, real company logo, real brand, trade mark, celebrity, recognisable face

by_kind.prop: background clutter, other objects, multiple objects, second object, duplicate, cropped object, cut off edges, ground shadow, cast shadow, harsh shadow, contact shadow, reflections, mirror, text, lettering, numbers, label, room, interior, table, floor boards, street scene, buildings, horizon, depth of field, blurred edges, vignette, extreme wide angle, fisheye
